scope: Recommendations only; no main artifact or model edits. Ten substantive main pages, no added cover. Read current screen, notes 9–10, demand and valuation audits, and independent root counterexample audit; incorporated new findings communicated by the demand and valuation agents.
central_revision: Defend an observed premium-product transition that may persist, then show how its economics reach shareholders and determine entry. The growth-through-share-loss identity is a supporting calculation, not the entire affirmative case.

positive_basis: Intel reported Q3 server ASP growth of 54% and units growth of 10% year over year; most ASP improvement reflected premium mix, with higher unit costs. This is Intel-specific evidence that the hypothesized mechanism is already operating.
Derived CPU sales rose from $4.12B in Q1 to $5.92B in Q3; Q4 DCAI guidance calls for mid-teens sequential growth. This supports a stronger exit run-rate, although the CPU allocation is modeled.

Intel's Q1 prepared remarks report signed DCAI long-term agreements, including Google; Google's own April 22 compute post confirms expanded Granite Rapids deployments. These support multi-period adoption, without disclosing contracted volumes, realized prices, or Intel margins.

The forecast therefore prefers continuation of observed premium-product adoption, not extrapolation of the 54% growth rate. Its exact exit anchor and subsequent ramp remain choices requiring corroboration.
rational_forecast_defense.what_this_changes: The defense can explain why it favors persistence over normalization. It no longer depends only on saying the forecast is possible or caveated. That is a rational underwriting argument; it does not establish a statistically calibrated probability or prove that 21.9% is uniquely correct.
rational_forecast_defense.what_it_does_not_change: The current quote still fails the chosen hurdles. Higher costs, competitive capture, and long-run reinvestment can prevent richer mix from becoming shareholder value. No target increase is justified by this wording improvement alone.

main_deck_plan.change: Surface today's no-initiation decision beside the conditional long and dated target. State premium-mix persistence and consolidated cash conversion as the actual bets.
main_deck_plan.why: The reader should know both the affirmative operating view and the current security decision immediately.

main_deck_plan.change: Keep the shipment and revenue bridges. Pair the 10% ASP counterexample with the flat-modeled-Q4-ASP control and explain that 10% annual ASP implies approximately 6% below the modeled Q4 level.
main_deck_plan.why: Identifies the competing economic regimes instead of allowing '10% growth' to sound like merely a smaller incremental increase above exit.

main_deck_plan.change: Replace the right-hand arithmetic bullets with observed evidence → economic mechanism → forecast choice. Retain the left quarterly chart and H1 test.
main_deck_plan.why: Affirmative evidence should explain why the candidate carries the ramp forward; the existing chart already supplies the arithmetic.

main_deck_plan.change: Replace reverse-cash requirements with returns at $40 under the core, higher-rate core, chosen stress, funded CPU-plus-factory setback, lower case, and adverse case. Make the bottom panel an evidence-conditioned decision rule.
main_deck_plan.why: Shows the actual risk accepted at the proposed entry. Reverse-cash math is already available in defense notes.

main_deck_plan.change: Replace the full borrowing-rate page with recurring 2030 EBIT-to-parent-cash bridges for the core and the funded combined setback. Keep one compact funding box and a duration/reinvestment statement.
main_deck_plan.why: Profit retention and recurring cash are central to the thesis; a few hundredths of target-price financing sensitivity are not.

main_deck_plan.change: Retain the contrary workload evidence with its existing scope. Do not claim that it independently sets Intel's global share loss.
main_deck_plan.why: It demonstrates evidence discipline and tests a broad cost-leadership claim without pretending to provide the bullish forecast.

causal_underwriting_rows.observed_evidence: Q3 server ASP +54%, units +10% YoY; premium mix drove most ASP improvement, alongside higher unit costs.
causal_underwriting_rows.mechanism: Richer packages raise revenue per processor even while shipment share falls.
causal_underwriting_rows.forecast_choice: Retain the modeled Q4 mix level and add modest further in-year mix gains; core 2027 average ASP is 21.9% above the 2026 average.
causal_underwriting_rows.discriminating_test: Rebuild Q4 CPU revenue and confront the implied unit/ASP split with disclosed changes. Revenue alone cannot validate both inputs.

causal_underwriting_rows.observed_evidence: Signed DCAI long-term agreements including Google; customer-confirmed Granite Rapids deployment expansion.
causal_underwriting_rows.mechanism: A product transition embedded in customer deployments can persist across reporting periods.
causal_underwriting_rows.forecast_choice: Continue adoption into the 2027 ramp and the separate 2028 unit/mix assumptions; agreements do not establish the quantities.
causal_underwriting_rows.discriminating_test: Q4 CPU sales $6.81B and H1 2027 $14.11B test the delivery path; rebase misses without automatic catch-up.

causal_underwriting_rows.observed_evidence: Foundry losses have narrowed and management reports lower node costs; the improvements already appear in current results.
causal_underwriting_rows.mechanism: More saleable output and lower costs can let product profit survive manufacturing losses and capital requirements.
causal_underwriting_rows.forecast_choice: Retain $124.5B physical capex in 2027–30; core 2030 parent operating cash is $19.45B before finite credits and financing.
causal_underwriting_rows.discriminating_test: Require consolidated EBIT and cash conversion, not product-segment margin alone. The 2028 core has $24.59B group EBIT and $3.75B parent unlevered cash, but that cash includes $6.17B finite credits; excluding them it is -$2.42B. Do not call positive 2028 total cash proof of recurring cash generation.

pricing_counterexample_answer.answer: The counterexample identifies the right bet: whether Intel retains its richer Xeon mix. My preference for persistence has evidence behind it. Q3 server ASP rose 54% and units 10%; Intel attributes most ASP improvement to premium mix. It has also signed DCAI long-term agreements, including Google, and Google has expanded Granite Rapids deployments. I am not extrapolating 54% growth. Conditional on my Q4 exit estimate, holding ASP flat through 2027 still leaves company sales around 2.7% above consensus, and about 5.5% above in 2028 with the same later growth assumptions. The 10% annual-ASP case instead implies roughly 6% below that estimated Q4 level. So it tests a weaker exit anchor or mix normalization. I prefer continuation of the observed product transition, but I will rebase the forecast if Q4 pricing, units, and H1 delivery fail to support it.
pricing_counterexample_answer.judge_follow_up: Your Q4 level is still an estimate. Why should I favor that anchor over the 10% case?
pricing_counterexample_answer.answer_to_follow_up: Because the recent Intel-specific evidence shows rising premium-product adoption and customer commitments, while 10% is an illustrative normalization assumption rather than a measured price outlook. That gives the continuation case a positive rationale; it does not prove its exact magnitude. The $6.81B Q4 CPU estimate is a favorable allocation of DCAI guidance, so I must test it against the actual CPU residual and reported unit/mix disclosures. If the anchor fails, I lower the future base rather than preserve the target through assumed catch-up.
pricing_counterexample_answer.boundary: Do not compare Q3 +54% YoY directly with 2027 +21.9% annual ASP as if they use the same base. Do not call signed agreements contracted revenue, a price floor, or verified margins. The flat-Q4 control remains conditional on an estimated Q4 level and preserves later forecast growth.

combined_setback_answer.answer: The combined setback changes the decision, and I have now funded it rather than adding standalone losses. With the CPU delay layered onto the factory, terminal-return, and higher-rate stress, the model retains $124.5B of near-term capex, draws about $2.65B, and repays in Q4 2028. The funded target is about $59.50, giving 10.0% annually from $40. That is below my chosen 12% stress hurdle. This does not make the combined outcome the expected case, but it means $40 cannot be an automatic buy after that delivery setback. My rule is to rebuild sales, recurring cash, funding, and the remaining horizon before setting the limit. The operating mechanism can survive while the investable price changes. The approximately $37.17 ceiling is a diagnostic for this case, not a new recommendation.
combined_setback_answer.judge_follow_up: Why retain a $40 headline when a fairly ordinary delay breaks its selected stress hurdle?
combined_setback_answer.answer_to_follow_up: Because $40 describes the current reference-case decision, conditional on its operating evidence, rather than a promise to buy whenever the tape touches it. But the combination shows that its cushion is narrow. I would remove any wording suggesting a robust downside floor, keep the combined case beside the selected one, and let the revised forecast set the entry. If I cannot defend the faster operating path after the new evidence, I cannot keep the old limit.
combined_setback_answer.boundary: No rule says every downside must earn 12%. A hypothetical setback does not automatically become the underwriting case, but an observed or newly expected setback must change the inputs. Revolver capacity is disclosed; future access and assumed financing terms remain conditional.

entry_rule.plain_language: Initiate only if the latest higher-rate core clears 15% and the latest selected stress clears 12%, with CPU delivery, profit conversion, and funding re-underwritten. Recompute the remaining time to December 2030. The November 6 reference ceiling rounds down to $40; material adverse evidence can lower it.
entry_rule.substantive_condition: Latest targets must incorporate changed operating assumptions. 'Thesis intact' cannot mean only that Intel can still grow while losing share.
entry_rule.do_not_add: Do not add a mechanically inferred stop-loss, assign invented scenario probabilities, or turn every temporary quarterly variance into a permanent revenue haircut.

source_and_calculation_handoffs.source_limit: The demand agent verified the new primary-source statements. This subagent did not re-browse those pages; builder source insertion should follow the demand agent's captured provenance.

avoid: Calling a model reconciliation new evidence for its inputs
Reducing the pitch to repeated disclaimers without explaining the preferred economic mechanism
Calling the conditional recommendation a rule violation
Implying every adverse scenario must clear the selected hurdle
Treating the strongest possible honest presentation as a guaranteed winning pitch
Inflating value, lowering required returns, or concealing the lower cases to make the recommendation look stronger
